newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures slash gains late, end higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures slash gains late, end higher.

text.p: A late-afternoon spate of local and big dealer selling slashed hefty gains in U.S. debt futures, leaving most units only slightly higher on the day.

Traders said the pullback, which occurred during the last hour as trade turned busy again, wiped out the bulk of the day's gains as March Treasury bond futures hit big sell-stops after ticking back below intraday support near 110-20/32 and 110-16/32.
"It was local selling first," said one floor broker. "Then it got below 16 (110-16/32)...it didn't feel good there and they sold the hell out of it."
"There was talk of a big seller of 10-years (Treasury notes) and the 30-year in cash," said another broker.
He said cash pressure spilled over, with three dealers selling 3,000 to 4,000 March futures apiece on the late fall.

The market, already in the throes of an active selloff, paid less heed than it otherwise might have to the 0.8-percent rise in Redbook Research's retail sales index during the first three weeks of January versus December, brokers said.
Some brokers said the late gain-cutting positioned March T-bond futures for a lower start Wednesday. "It sets it up for a poor opening tomorrow," said the second broker.
Futures spiked up early when the fourth-quarter U.S. employment cost index rose 0.8 percent against consensus forecasts for a 0.9 percent gain. ECI in the third quarter rose 0.6 percent.
Brokers said the tame rise in the wage-inflation barometer made it less likely the Federal Reserve would feel the need to hike rates at the policy-making arm's meeting February 4-5.

March T-bonds ended up 9/32 at 110-02/32, 10-year notes rose 6/32 to 107-29/32, muni-bonds added 9/32 to 113-31/32, June T-bills rose two bps to 94.92, and June Eurodollars gained five bps to 94.20. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
